title: This Garden Songbird Flies Into Caves to Kill Bats

scenes.text: A garden songbird that hunts bats.
The great tit. Five inches long, a bird-feeder regular. In a cave in Hungary, it turned predator.
Scientists watched for two winters. The birds flew into the dark, found hibernating pipistrelle bats, and killed them. Seventeen kills counted.
How does a bird find a bat in the dark? It listens. Disturbed bats squeak, and the tits home in on the sound.
A catch took fifteen minutes at most. Some birds carried the bat out to a tree to eat it.
Then the scientists hung up sunflower seeds and bacon fat. The hunting stopped. It was never bloodlust. It was hunger.

description:
Great tits, the common garden songbird, were filmed flying into a Hungarian cave to hunt, kill and eat hibernating pipistrelle bats.
Over two winters researchers counted 17 kills on days without a feeder; the birds found the bats by their squeaks and even flew toward a speaker playing the sounds. When sunflower seeds and bacon fat were hung near the cave, the bat hunting almost completely stopped. Published in Biology Letters in 2009.
What is the most unexpected predator you have seen in your garden?
subject: great tit bird
first_comment: The bats were still groggy from hibernation, which is why a five-inch songbird could take them. Which other harmless-looking animal has a dark side?
